title: 2002 AMC 12A Problem 16
statement: Tina randomly selects two distinct numbers from the set \(\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\},\) and Sergio randomly selects a number from the set \(\{1, 2, \ldots, 10\}.\) The probability that Sergio’s number is larger than the sum of the two numbers chosen by Tina is

solutions.text:
Tina’s ten pairs have sums \(3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 9.\) For a sum \(s,\) Sergio’s number exceeds it with probability \(\dfrac{10 - s}{10}.\)

The corresponding values of \(10 - s\) are \(7, 6, 5, 5, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 1,\) totaling \(40.\) The overall probability is \(\dfrac{40}{10\cdot 10} = \dfrac{2}{5}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: For a pair with sum \(s,\) Sergio exceeds it with probability \(\dfrac{10 - s}{10}\)
